questions.prompt: Why is multi-model architecture recommended for enterprise production environments?
options: It isolates failure domains and access boundaries between data tiers, apps, and monitoring while allowing integration via CMR
Because Juju controllers only support a single application per model
To reduce network bandwidth usage across physical switches
To bypass Juju's limit on maximum relation counts
questions.answer: It isolates failure domains and access boundaries between data tiers, apps, and monitoring while allowing integration via CMR
questions.explanation: Multi-model architecture isolates operational risk and permissions across tiers (e.g. data vs frontend) while enabling secure cross-model integrations.

questions.prompt: What is a recommended practice when defining charm channels in production manifests?
options: Always lock charm deployments to explicit tracks and risk channels (e.g. 14/stable)
Always use the edge channel to receive unreleased fixes immediately
Omit the channel entirely so Juju selects arbitrary builds
Deploy charms only from local zip archives uploaded over SSH
questions.answer: Always lock charm deployments to explicit tracks and risk channels (e.g. 14/stable)
questions.explanation: Pinning explicit tracks (e.g., 14/stable or 8.0/stable) prevents accidental breaking upgrades.

questions.prompt: How can CI/CD pipelines detect configuration and topology drift in Juju environments?
options: By running scheduled 'terraform plan -detailed-exitcode' or automated JSON status assertions
By taking daily screenshots of the web terminal
By checking the controller system uptime with ping
By restarting the controller daemon every 12 hours
questions.answer: By running scheduled 'terraform plan -detailed-exitcode' or automated JSON status assertions
questions.explanation: Automated Terraform plans or status assertions compare actual model state against declared manifests to identify drift.
